title: Best Massage Guns UK
short: Percussion massage guns compared by power, attachments and portability, from compact minis to premium investment models.
intro: A massage gun's deep vibrations help ease tight muscles and DOMS after training, but size, power and attachments vary hugely between models. This guide compares massage guns tested by Women's Running's panel through real marathon training and daily use.

products.name: Q2 Pro Mini
products.best_for: Runners who want a portable gun that doesn't skimp on features
products.summary: Women's Running's tester called this the most brilliant bit of recovery kit tested in a long time, neat enough to carry around without feeling heavy, with good range of movement to reach sore spots. The heat-and-cold head stood out as a favourite feature, described as a game changer for DOMS during marathon training.
pros: Comfortable grip, even on full power

products.name: Massage Gun with Heat and Cold
products.best_for: Buyers who want app guidance and both hot and cold therapy
products.key_spec: 5 attachment heads with hot-and-cold, companion app, LCD screen
products.summary: A versatile gun that Women's Running found worked well across five speed settings for easing sore muscles, with a hot-and-cool head that warmed and cooled almost instantaneously. An LCD screen shows speed and battery level, and the companion app offers guided videos for using the gun on different muscle areas.
pros: Helpful LCD screen with battery indicator

products.name: L7 Ultra
products.best_for: Runners who struggle to massage their own back and shoulders
products.key_spec: 0.6kg, extension handle, infrared heat and red light therapy head
products.summary: Women's Running's tester called this a game-changer for reaching the back without a willing partner, thanks to a clever extension handle that turns it from a mini gun into a full-reach tool. An infrared heat head warms sore muscles and is said to promote faster recovery, particularly praised for tight shoulders and lats.

specs.Attachment heads: 5, including infrared heat and red light

pros: Extension handle reaches the whole back

products.name: Hypervolt 2 Pro
products.best_for: Serious or daily users who want maximum power
products.summary: Used daily on legs during a 70-day running streak, Women's Running's tester found this delivered far more powerful massage than an older gun used for years, rarely needing to go above speed three out of five. Described as 'the Rolls Royce of massagers', it's heavier during extended use, though easy enough to switch hands.

guide.a: A mini gun, like the Bob and Brad Q2 Pro here, is lighter and more portable for gym bags or travel, and is often enough power for home use. A full-size gun, like the Hyperice Hypervolt 2 Pro, is typically more powerful and better suited to daily use on larger muscle groups or if you want maximum intensity.

guide.q: How often should I use a massage gun?
guide.a: A massage gun can be used once a day for general muscle care and prevention, or up to three times a day when muscles are especially sore. As a rule of thumb, limit use to a maximum of two minutes on any single muscle group per session.

guide.q: Is a heat-and-cold head worth it?
guide.a: A heated head, like those on the Bob and Brad or RENPHO guns here, can help warm up muscles before a run, while a cold setting soothes and aids recovery afterwards. It's a genuinely useful two-in-one feature if you want both pre- and post-run muscle care from one device.

guide.q: Do I need an app-connected massage gun?
guide.a: An app, like RENPHO's here, adds guided videos showing how to use the gun on different muscle groups, which is useful if you're new to percussion massage. If you already know your usual trouble spots, a simpler gun without app connectivity covers the same core function.
